$comment: Makerspace Standards of Excellence. Lifted from the original single-file tool (makehaven/Makerspace-Standards) by scripts/extract-standards.mjs on 2026-10-08. A changed standard or anchor is a new framework version; assessments record the version they were made against.

flags.label: Hosts repair cafés or salvage programs?
Rents dedicated desks, studios, bays, storage?
At least 3 years of retained records?

standards.text: Legal entity, tax-exempt status, registrations, and required filings are current.
standards.evidence: Formation documents; determination letter; filing calendar; latest filings
anchors: No formation documents on hand; filing status unknown or lapsed.
Incorporated and tax-exempt, but filings are tracked informally and documents are scattered.
All registrations current; a filing calendar exists and the latest filings are on file.
Several years of on-time filings; the calendar has an owner and is reviewed annually.

standards.text: Governing documents define authority, elections, meetings, and dissolution.
anchors: No bylaws can be produced, or practice ignores them.
Bylaws exist but are outdated or silent on elections, meetings, or dissolution.
Current bylaws cover authority, elections, meetings, and dissolution; amendments are recorded.
Bylaws are reviewed on a set cycle; amendment history is documented in minutes.

standards.text: Board has at least five independent, unrelated voting directors or documents why another structure is appropriate.
anchors: Fewer than five directors, or mostly related people, with no documented rationale.
Board is near the bar but independence has never been documented.
Roster shows five or more independent, unrelated directors with declarations — or a documented rationale for another structure.
Independence is reaffirmed annually and recruitment sustains the standard.

standards.text: Board meets regularly and retains approved minutes documenting decisions.
anchors: Meetings are irregular and minutes are missing.
Board meets, but minutes are inconsistent or never formally approved.
Regular meeting calendar; approved minutes document every decision.
A multi-year archive of approved minutes makes past decisions easy to retrieve.

standards.text: Conflict-of-interest policy includes annual disclosure and documented handling of conflicts.
anchors: No conflict-of-interest policy.
A policy exists but annual disclosures are not collected.
Annual signed disclosures; conflicts are handled and recorded in minutes.
Several years of disclosures on file; handling is reviewed for effectiveness.

standards.text: Whistleblower, records-retention, and ethics policies cover directors, staff, and key volunteers.
anchors: None of these policies exist.
One or two exist but coverage is partial and training is absent.
Board-approved whistleblower, records-retention, and ethics policies with training records.
Policies are reviewed on a cycle and training is refreshed and logged.

standards.text: Board-approved strategy connects mission, programs, facilities, and major capital purchases.
standards.evidence: Strategic plan; annual goals; board review
anchors: No strategy beyond day-to-day survival.
Goals live informally with a few leaders.
A board-approved plan connects mission, programs, facilities, and capital purchases, with annual goals.
The plan is reviewed annually against results and cited in major decisions.

standards.text: Users retain intellectual property they create except where a written agreement clearly states otherwise.
anchors: No position on who owns what users create.
Informal understanding that users keep their IP; nothing written.
A written IP policy plus a sponsored-project agreement template are in use.
The policy is periodically reviewed and agreements are consistently executed.

standards.text: Leadership succession and emergency authority are documented and tested.
standards.evidence: Succession plan; delegation matrix; test record
anchors: No plan for leadership absence or emergency authority.
Key knowledge is held by individuals; emergency authority is undocumented.
A succession plan and delegation matrix are documented.
The plan has been tested by drill or a real absence and updated afterward.

standards.text: Board completes a documented annual self-evaluation and reviews organizational risk.
standards.evidence: Three annual evaluations; risk register reviews
anchors: No board self-evaluation or risk review.
Occasional informal reflection, nothing documented.
A documented annual self-evaluation and organizational risk review.
Three consecutive annual evaluations with follow-up actions tracked.

standards.text: Written general safety rules, emergency procedures, and emergency contacts are visible and current.
standards.evidence: Safety manual; posted procedures; review date
anchors: No written safety rules.
Rules exist but are outdated or not visible in the shop.
Current rules, emergency procedures, and contacts are posted with a review date.
Reviews happen on schedule and updates are logged.

standards.text: Required fire protection, first-aid supplies, eyewash, exits, and emergency shutoffs are accessible and inspected.
anchors: Extinguishers, first aid, or eyewash missing, blocked, or expired.
Equipment is present but inspections are ad hoc.
An inspection checklist with current service tags; everything accessible.
Multi-year inspection records; deficiencies tracked to correction.

standards.text: Hazardous chemicals are labeled, stored compatibly, and supported by accessible SDS information.
standards.evidence: Chemical inventory; SDS access; storage inspection
anchors: Unlabeled containers or incompatible storage.
Most chemicals labeled; SDS collection incomplete.
Inventory maintained, SDS accessible, storage compatibility verified.
Storage is audited periodically and the inventory reconciled yearly.

standards.text: Tools have point-of-use rules and required guarding, dust collection, ventilation, and PPE.
anchors: Guards removed or missing; no point-of-use rules.
Some tool SOPs exist; PPE and dust collection are inconsistent.
SOPs posted at tools; guarding, dust collection, ventilation, and PPE in place and inspected.
Inspections are logged over time and SOPs updated after incidents.

standards.text: Tools are assigned risk levels that determine training, supervision, and access-control requirements.
anchors: No notion of tool risk levels.
An informal sense of which tools are dangerous guides practice.
A hazard matrix ties each tool risk level to training, supervision, and access control.
The matrix is reviewed and access rules are audited against it.

standards.text: Injuries, near misses, unsafe conditions, and equipment damage are promptly reported and reviewed.
anchors: Incidents go unrecorded.
Serious injuries get mentioned; near misses are lost.
A reporting form and log capture injuries, near misses, and damage, with corrective actions.
Trends are analyzed and recurring causes demonstrably addressed.

standards.text: Opening, closing, lone-work, impairment, and after-hours emergency protocols are documented.
anchors: No documented protocols.
Practices exist by habit; nothing written.
Opening, closing, lone-work, impairment, and after-hours protocols are documented and taught.
Protocols are reviewed and updated from real events.

standards.text: Insurance coverages and limits are reviewed annually against actual operations.
anchors: Coverage unknown or lapsed.
Policies in force but never compared to actual operations.
An annual broker review matches coverage to operations; the board is informed.
Multi-year review records show changes made from findings.

standards.text: A qualified annual safety audit tracks findings through closure and analyzes incident trends.
standards.evidence: Three annual audits; closure log; trend review
anchors: No safety audit has ever happened.
Occasional informal walkthroughs.
A qualified annual audit with findings tracked to closure.
Three annual audits plus a closure log and incident-trend analysis.

standards.text: Waste, emissions, used materials, and hazardous disposal are managed under documented environmental procedures.
standards.evidence: Waste plan; vendor records; training logs
anchors: Hazardous waste goes in the dumpster.
Disposal is roughly right but undocumented.
A written waste plan, vendor records, and training logs.
Practices are reviewed and improved; records span multiple years.

standards.text: Every member completes orientation, accepts conduct rules, and signs required agreements before access.
anchors: People get access without orientation or signatures.
Orientation happens but records are spotty.
Checklist-based orientation with signed agreements before access; records kept.
Records are audited and orientation content is reviewed.

standards.text: Restricted tools require verified practical training before independent use.
anchors: Anyone can use any tool.
Training is expected but verification is informal.
Verified practical training is recorded before independent use of restricted tools.
Training records are sampled for quality and the curriculum reviewed.

standards.text: Digital or auditable credentials control tool and facility access and can be suspended promptly.
standards.evidence: Badge database; access-control test; suspension procedure
anchors: No way to tell who has access to what.
Shared keys or codes; suspension is slow or impossible.
Per-person auditable credentials control access; suspension works promptly.
Access rights are periodically audited against the credential database.

standards.text: Dues, holds, guests, refunds, accessibility accommodations, and termination rules are transparent.
anchors: Rules are invented case by case.
Policies exist but are not published.
Dues, holds, guests, refunds, accommodations, and termination rules are published.
Policies are reviewed and refined from member feedback.

standards.text: Conduct and disciplinary procedures provide reporting, fair review, documentation, and proportionate action.
standards.evidence: Conduct policy; complaint procedure; de-identified case log
anchors: No conduct procedure; issues are handled arbitrarily.
Issues handled ad hoc by whoever is present.
A written procedure covers reporting, fair review, documentation, and proportionate action.
A de-identified case log exists and the process is reviewed for fairness.

standards.text: Credential quality is periodically reviewed and portable credentials are accepted only through defined equivalency rules.
standards.evidence: Curriculum review; equivalency agreements; audit sample
anchors: Credential quality is never examined.
Instructors vary widely with no review.
Periodic curriculum review; outside credentials accepted only via defined equivalency rules.
Audit samples confirm credential quality over time.

standards.text: Visitors register, accept safety/conduct rules, and remain within defined access boundaries.
anchors: Visitors wander in unrecorded.
A sign-in sheet exists but is inconsistently used.
Registration, rules acceptance, and defined access boundaries are enforced.
Logs are reviewed and boundaries and signage refined.

standards.text: Staffing and supervision levels match the hazards available during public access.
anchors: Public hours run without hazard-matched supervision.
Staffing is set by availability, not hazards.
A coverage schedule matches supervision to the hazards available.
Coverage is reviewed against incidents and adjusted.

standards.text: Point-of-use authorization or verified workshop credentials govern restricted equipment use.
anchors: Visitors can reach restricted equipment unsupervised.
Staff intervene informally at risky tools.
Point-of-use authorization or verified workshop credentials govern restricted equipment.
Authorization records are kept and periodically checked.

standards.text: Accessible pathways help repeat visitors advance from introduction to independent capability.
anchors: No path beyond a first visit.
Repeat visitors advance only by asking around.
A documented pathway moves visitors from introduction toward independent capability.
Pathway completion is tracked and the design improved.

standards.text: Public-access data and feedback are reviewed to improve hours, staffing, access, and instruction.
anchors: No public-access data is collected.
Anecdotes drive decisions.
Data and feedback are reviewed annually to improve hours, staffing, and instruction.
Three annual reviews and a change log show decisions made from data.

standards.text: A current inventory identifies major equipment, location, status, and responsible lead.
anchors: No asset list exists.
A partial or stale spreadsheet.
A current register lists major equipment, location, status, and responsible lead.
The register is reconciled annually and discrepancies resolved.

standards.text: Unsafe equipment is clearly locked out and cannot return to service without authorization.
anchors: Broken tools stay in service or carry only a note.
Tagging is informal; returns to service are unverified.
A lockout procedure with authorization required before return to service; records kept.
Practice is audited and repeat failures analyzed.

standards.text: Preventive maintenance schedules reflect manufacturer guidance, use, and risk.
anchors: Equipment runs to failure.
Some machines get attention when someone remembers.
Schedules reflect manufacturer guidance, use, and risk, with completed logs.
Multi-year logs tune the schedule based on failure history.

standards.text: Original manuals, warranties, leases, insurance, access-control configuration, and critical records are securely backed up.
anchors: Critical documents exist only on paper or one laptop.
Some records backed up; coverage unknown.
An indexed document set is securely backed up and the backup tested.
Backups are tested on a schedule; the index stays current.

standards.text: Shop inspections verify egress, storage, guards, utilities, ventilation, and housekeeping.
anchors: No routine shop inspections.
Occasional informal walkarounds.
Routine checklists verify egress, storage, guards, utilities, ventilation, and housekeeping.
Inspection history shows findings closed out.

standards.text: Critical digital services have named owners, backups, recovery instructions, and controlled administrator access.
standards.evidence: Systems register; recovery test; admin roster
anchors: One person holds all the passwords.
A partial list of systems and owners; backups unverified.
A systems register with owners, tested backups, recovery instructions, and controlled admin access.
Recovery is re-tested periodically and admin access audited.

standards.text: Annual asset audits reconcile inventory, condition, maintenance, training controls, and replacement needs.
anchors: Assets are never audited.
Partial spot checks only.
An annual audit reconciles inventory, condition, maintenance, training controls, and replacement needs.
Three annual audits on file.

standards.text: A board-designated capital replacement plan and reserve reflect documented lifecycle needs.
anchors: No replacement planning or reserve.
Awareness of looming replacements, nothing designated.
A board-designated replacement plan and reserve reflect documented lifecycle needs.
The reserve is funded per forecast and reviewed annually.

standards.text: Board approves an annual budget and reviews timely budget-to-actual, balance sheet, and cash information.
anchors: No budget.
A budget is set but rarely revisited.
Approved budget with timely budget-to-actual, balance sheet, and cash review.
Multi-year discipline; variances explained and acted on.

standards.text: Financial duties are separated or compensating controls are documented for receipts, payments, payroll, and reconciliation.
anchors: One person handles money end to end, unchecked.
Some approvals exist; controls undocumented.
A control matrix documents separation or compensating controls, with reconciliation samples.
Controls are tested or reviewed periodically.

standards.text: Restricted funds, donations, acknowledgments, and fundraising claims are handled accurately.
anchors: Restricted gifts mix with general funds.
Donations acknowledged inconsistently.
Gift records, acknowledgments, and a restrictions schedule are accurate.
Restricted-fund handling is reviewed with no exceptions found.

standards.text: Board reviews liquidity, revenue concentration, liabilities, and insurance at least annually.
anchors: The board never sees financial risk.
Finances discussed without structure.
Liquidity, revenue concentration, liabilities, and insurance reviewed at least annually.
A standing dashboard and minuted risk discussions across years.

standards.text: Independent financial review, compilation, or audit matches legal requirements and organizational risk.
anchors: No independent financial review of any kind.
Internal review only.
Independent review, compilation, or audit matches legal requirements and risk; letters answered.
Recurring engagements with findings resolved.

standards.text: Multi-year forecasts and reserves demonstrate a credible continuity plan under adverse scenarios.
anchors: No forward look beyond this year.
A rough one-year projection.
Multi-year forecast, adverse-scenario analysis, and a reserve policy.
Updated annually and credible under stress-testing.

standards.text: Every employee has a current job description, lawful classification, payroll processing, and required postings.
standards.evidence: Job descriptions; payroll records; postings checklist
anchors: Classification or payroll basics are missing or wrong.
Payroll runs; job descriptions are stale.
Current job descriptions, lawful classification, payroll records, and required postings.
Reviewed annually as roles change.

standards.text: Employee handbook covers conduct, harassment, leave, hours, safety, complaints, and discipline.
anchors: No handbook.
A partial or outdated handbook.
Handbook covers conduct, harassment, leave, hours, safety, complaints, and discipline, with acknowledgments.
Updated on a cycle with training on changes.

standards.text: Performance goals, supervision, compensation review, and annual evaluations are documented.
anchors: No goals, supervision, or evaluations.
Feedback happens informally.
Documented goals, supervision, compensation review, and annual evaluations.
A consistent multi-year evaluation record.

standards.text: Leadership reviews retention, workload, pay equity, development, and single-person dependencies.
standards.evidence: Three annual workforce reviews; mitigation plan
anchors: Workforce risks are invisible.
Leadership discusses staffing informally.
A documented annual review of retention, workload, pay equity, development, and dependencies.
Three annual reviews with a mitigation plan.

standards.text: Volunteer leads have defined roles, authority, contacts, and required safety qualifications.
standards.evidence: Lead roster; role descriptions; training records
anchors: Whoever shows up runs things.
Lead roles are understood but undocumented.
A lead roster with role descriptions, authority, contacts, and safety qualifications.
Roles are reviewed and qualifications kept current.

standards.text: Scheduling, onboarding, supervision, complaints, removal, and escalation are documented.
anchors: No documented volunteer operations.
Practices exist by tradition.
Scheduling, onboarding, supervision, complaints, removal, and escalation are documented.
The handbook is maintained and applied consistently.

standards.text: Critical responsibilities have backup coverage and transitions do not depend on one volunteer.
anchors: Single points of failure everywhere.
A few roles have informal backups.
A coverage matrix and handoff documentation for critical responsibilities.
Transitions have happened smoothly using the documentation.

standards.text: Leadership annually reviews workload, retention, recognition, burnout risk, and succession.
anchors: Volunteer burnout and turnover are never examined.
Occasional informal check-ins.
A documented annual review of workload, retention, recognition, burnout, and succession.
Three annual reviews with improvement actions taken.

standards.text: Organization tracks who participates, what they use, and basic program attendance.
anchors: No participation records.
Headcounts sometimes taken.
Membership, visitor, and attendance reports are produced routinely.
Reports inform staffing and program decisions.

standards.text: Nondiscrimination, accessibility, and inclusion expectations apply to users, staff, volunteers, and programs.
anchors: No nondiscrimination or accessibility commitments.
A statement exists; no procedure or training.
Policies, an accommodation procedure, and training cover users, staff, volunteers, and programs.
Outcomes are monitored and the approach reviewed.

standards.text: Measurable annual goals connect activities to participant learning, agency, belonging, or opportunity.
anchors: Activities have no stated outcomes.
Aspirations are described but unmeasurable.
Measurable annual goals connect activities to learning, agency, belonging, or opportunity.
Targets are tracked across years and inform planning.

standards.text: Participant feedback is collected safely and reviewed with usage and demographic information.
anchors: Feedback is never collected.
Occasional surveys, rarely reviewed.
Feedback is collected safely and reviewed with usage and demographic information.
Multi-year feedback shapes documented changes.

standards.text: Instruction supports choice, iteration, peer learning, and multiple ways to participate and demonstrate learning.
standards.evidence: Facilitation guide; observation rubric; instructor training
anchors: Instruction is one-size-fits-all.
Some instructors use good practice on their own.
A facilitation guide, observation rubric, and instructor training support choice, iteration, and peer learning.
Instruction is observed and improved on a cycle.

standards.text: Community partnerships have clear purposes, responsibilities, and mutual benefit.
anchors: Partnerships are handshakes.
Partners exist without defined responsibilities.
MOUs define purpose, responsibilities, and mutual benefit.
Partnerships are reviewed and renewed deliberately.

standards.text: A public annual report summarizes finances, participation, outcomes, setbacks, and improvement commitments.
anchors: No public reporting.
Occasional updates without finances or outcomes.
An annual public report covers finances, participation, outcomes, and setbacks.
Three annual reports on file.

standards.text: Evaluation findings demonstrably influence program design, outreach, staffing, and capital decisions.
anchors: Evaluation never changes anything.
Findings occasionally spark change, undocumented.
Findings visibly influence programs, outreach, staffing, and capital decisions.
A three-year decision log ties changes to evidence.

standards.text: Each circulating tool is uniquely identified and checked out to a verified borrower.
anchors: No record of what left the building.
A paper list of loans, often stale.
Each tool is uniquely identified and checked out to a verified borrower.
Checkout records are audited against inventory.

standards.text: Loan agreement, due dates, condition, accessories, loss, and safe-use limits are documented.
anchors: No loan agreement.
A basic form missing key terms.
Agreement covers due dates, condition, accessories, loss, and safe-use limits.
Terms are reviewed from real loss and dispute experience.

standards.text: Returned powered tools receive documented functional and electrical inspection before recirculation.
anchors: Returned tools go straight back on the shelf.
Visual check only.
Documented functional and electrical inspection before recirculation.
Inspection logs are complete and reviewed.

standards.text: Loss, damage, late return, utilization, and maintenance trends inform inventory decisions.
anchors: Lending performance is unknown.
Losses noticed anecdotally.
Loss, damage, late-return, utilization, and maintenance trends are tracked.
Three annual analyses inform inventory decisions.

standards.text: Parent/guardian consent, emergency contacts, supervision, and authorized pickup rules are enforced.
anchors: Youth participate without consent forms.
Forms collected inconsistently.
Consent, emergency contacts, supervision, and pickup rules are enforced with complete records.
Rosters and forms are audited by sample.

standards.text: Age and capability rules prohibit or control youth access to hazardous equipment.
anchors: No age rules around hazardous equipment.
Informal judgment calls.
An age and capability matrix controls youth access to hazardous equipment.
The matrix is reviewed with curricula and incidents.

standards.text: Background screening and youth-protection training apply to all covered adults before service.
anchors: Unscreened adults work with youth.
Some screening; coverage incomplete.
Background screening and youth-protection training precede service for all covered adults.
A roster tracks renewals with no lapses.

standards.text: Two-adult/open-observable practices, reporting duties, communication, and overnight/transport rules are documented as applicable.
anchors: No youth-protection practices documented.
Two-adult practice by custom only.
Two-adult and open-observable practices, reporting duties, and communication rules are documented.
Practices are trained, followed, and reviewed.

standards.text: Youth curricula and outcomes are periodically reviewed with educators, families, and participants.
anchors: Youth programming is never reviewed.
Informal debriefs only.
Curricula and outcomes are reviewed with educators, families, and participants.
Three annual reviews with changes made.

standards.text: Commercial use, production limits, shared-tool priority, staging, and prohibited activities are clear.
anchors: Commercial use is unregulated.
Informal expectations only.
A commercial-use policy covers limits, priority, staging, and prohibited activities.
The policy is enforced and reviewed.

standards.text: Written agreements define space, term, fees, insurance, IP, milestones, and termination.
anchors: Incubation runs on verbal deals.
Some agreements, missing key terms.
Written agreements define space, term, fees, insurance, IP, milestones, and termination.
Agreements and certificates are current and audited.

standards.text: Production activities receive documented safety, zoning, environmental, and capacity review.
anchors: Production starts without any review.
Ad hoc safety conversations.
Documented safety, zoning, environmental, and capacity review before production.
Reviews recur as activities change.

standards.text: Program outcomes and community subsidy are measured and reviewed for mission alignment.
standards.evidence: Three annual cohort and subsidy analyses
anchors: Program impact and subsidy are unknown.
Anecdotal wins only.
Outcomes and community subsidy are measured and reviewed for mission alignment.
Three annual cohort and subsidy analyses.

standards.text: Repair events use intake, ownership, safety, and liability procedures.
anchors: Repair events run without intake or waivers.
A sign-in sheet at best.
Intake, ownership, safety, and liability procedures are used at every event.
Procedures are refined from event experience.

standards.text: Repairs are assigned to qualified mentors and powered items receive an appropriate post-repair safety check.
anchors: Anyone repairs anything; items leave untested.
Skilled people gravitate to repairs informally.
Qualified mentors are assigned and powered items get a post-repair safety check.
Test logs are complete and reviewed.

standards.text: Salvaged materials are screened for hazardous coatings, contamination, structural defects, and prohibited items.
anchors: Salvage is accepted sight unseen.
Obvious hazards turned away informally.
A written acceptance policy screens coatings, contamination, defects, and prohibited items.
Inspection records show consistent screening.

standards.text: Diversion, repair outcomes, incidents, and repeat failures are reviewed annually.
anchors: Repair outcomes are never totaled.
Rough counts kept sometimes.
Diversion, outcomes, incidents, and repeat failures are reviewed annually.
Three annual outcome reports.

standards.text: Every occupant has a written license or rental agreement defining use, fees, term, termination, and non-subletting.
anchors: Occupants hold space on verbal arrangements.
Some agreements are written; terms vary.
Every occupant has a written agreement covering use, fees, term, termination, and non-subletting.
Agreements and the roster are reconciled on renewal.

standards.text: Egress, fire access, storage, chemicals, and housekeeping are inspected in private areas.
anchors: Private areas are never inspected.
Inspections only after complaints.
Egress, fire access, storage, chemicals, and housekeeping are inspected in private areas.
Logs show findings corrected.

standards.text: Electrical loads, personal machinery, alterations, hot work, and prohibited uses require defined approval.
anchors: Occupants modify and install freely.
Risky work is discouraged informally.
Electrical loads, machinery, alterations, hot work, and prohibited uses require defined approval.
Approval records are complete and reviewed.

standards.text: Access, property risk, required insurance, disputes, and abandoned property are addressed in writing.
anchors: Insurance, disputes, and abandoned property are unaddressed.
Handled case by case.
Access, property risk, required insurance, disputes, and abandoned property are covered in writing.
Provisions are exercised and refined as cases arise.

standards.text: Annual portfolio review covers compliance, incidents, insurance, occupancy, subsidy, and mission alignment.
anchors: The rental program is never reviewed.
Occupancy tracked, nothing else.
An annual review covers compliance, incidents, insurance, occupancy, subsidy, and mission alignment.
Three annual reviews on file.

standards.text: Organization participates in peer makerspace networks and shares documentation, curricula, or lessons learned beyond its own walls.
standards.evidence: Network memberships; shared templates or curricula; exchange or conference participation
anchors: The space operates in isolation from other makerspaces.
Individuals attend meetups or online forums informally; nothing organizational.
The organization belongs to at least one peer network and contributes documents, curricula, or data to it.
Sustained two-way participation: resources are both adopted from and contributed to the network over multiple years.
